question: A situation marked by rising prices and stagnation in demand is known as- (RRB JE (29/05/2019) Shift 3 CBT 1)
options: Demand–pull inflation
Wage–push inflation
Stagflation
Cost-push inflation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Stagflation

Explanation:
Stagflation is an economic situation characterized by simultaneously high inflation and high unemployment, along with stagnant demand. This condition typically arises from supply-side shocks, such as a sudden increase in oil prices. The term became prominent after the oil crisis of the 1970s. Unlike demand-pull inflation or cost-push inflation, stagflation combines recession with inflation, challenging traditional economic theories. It is particularly difficult to address because policies to reduce inflation may worsen unemployment and vice versa.

☛ What is the main problem in stagflation? → High inflation and high unemployment together
☛ What is a major cause of stagflation? → Supply-side shocks
☛ What happens to demand during stagflation? → Stagnant or low
☛ Which decade is the most famous example of stagflation? → The 1970s
question_hi: बढ़ती हुई कीमतों और मांग में स्थिरता द्वारा प्रदर्शित स्थिति को किस रूप में जाना जाता है? (RRB JE (29/05/2019) Shift 3 CBT 1)

Explanation:
मुद्रास्फीतिजनित मंदी (स्टैगफ्लेशन) एक आर्थिक स्थिति है जिसमें बेरोजगारी और मुद्रास्फीति एक साथ उच्च होती हैं, जबकि मांग स्थिर या कम होती है। यह स्थिति आमतौर पर आपूर्ति पक्ष के झटकों के कारण उत्पन्न होती है, जैसे तेल की कीमतों में अचानक वृद्धि। 1970 के दशक में तेल संकट के बाद यह शब्द प्रचलित हुआ। मांग-आधारित मुद्रास्फीति और लागत-आधारित मुद्रास्फीति से भिन्न, स्टैगफ्लेशन में मंदी और मुद्रास्फीति दोनों एक साथ होते हैं, जो पारंपरिक आर्थिक सिद्धांतों को चुनौती देते हैं।

question: Which of the following denotes currency with the public? (RRB JE CBT I (31/05/2019) Shift 1)
options: M3
M2
M4
M1
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is M1

Explanation:
There are four main measures of money supply: M1, M2, M3, and M4. Among these, M1 is the most liquid and narrow definition, representing currency with the public. It includes currency (notes and coins) held by the public and demand deposits (current and savings accounts) in banks. M1 is also called Narrow Money. In contrast, M2 adds post office savings accounts to M1, M3 includes time deposits along with M1 (called Broad Money), and M4 adds post office time deposits to M3. Thus, only M1 denotes the currency immediately available with the public for transactions.

☛ What does M1 include? → Currency with public and demand deposits
☛ What is M3 called? → Broad Money
☛ How does M2 differ from M1? → M2 includes post office savings deposits
☛ Who publishes money supply measures in India? → Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन जनता के पास मौजूद मुद्रा को दर्शाता है? (RRB JE CBT I (31/05/2019) Shift 1)
options_hi: M3
M2
M4
M1
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है M1

Explanation:
मुद्रा आपूर्ति के चार मुख्य स्तर हैं: M1, M2, M3 और M4। इनमें से M1 सबसे तरल और संकरी परिभाषा है, जो जनता के पास मौजूद मुद्रा को दर्शाता है। इसमें जनता के पास रखी करेंसी (नोट और सिक्के) और डिमांड डिपॉजिट (बैंकों में चालू खाते व बचत खाते) शामिल होते हैं। M1 को संकीर्ण मुद्रा (Narrow Money) भी कहा जाता है। वहीं M2 में M1 के साथ पोस्ट ऑफिस बचत खाते जुड़ते हैं, M3 में M1 के अलावा सावधि जमा (Time Deposits) शामिल होते हैं, और M4 में M3 के साथ पोस्ट ऑफिस सावधि जमा जुड़ते हैं। इस प्रकार केवल M1 ही जनता के पास तुरंत उपलब्ध मुद्रा को दर्शाता है।

question: Which of the following states recorded a population of more than 10 crore in the Census of India 2011? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 1)

Explanation:

question: In 1991, in order to make international adjustment the rupee was:  (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: stabilised
appreciated
printed
devalued
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is devalued

Explanation:
In 1991, India faced a severe balance of payments crisis, with foreign exchange reserves nearly exhausted. To tackle this, the government initiated economic reforms, and a key step was the devaluation of the rupee. Devaluation made exports cheaper and imports more expensive, helping to reduce the trade deficit and stabilize foreign reserves. This was done under the conditions set by the International Monetary Fund (IMF). The devaluation reduced the rupee's purchasing power in global markets but was crucial for restoring confidence in the Indian economy. It marked the beginning of India's economic liberalization. The rupee was devalued in two phases, totaling about 18-19% against the US dollar.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What caused the 1991 economic crisis in India? → Severe balance of payments problem and low foreign exchange reserves
☛ By what percentage was the rupee devalued in 1991? → About 18-19% (in two steps)
☛ Who was the Finance Minister of India at that time? → Dr. Manmohan Singh
☛ What was the effect of devaluation on exports? → Exports became more competitive, leading to an increase
☛ Against which currency did the rupee depreciate after devaluation? → US Dollar
question_hi: 1991 में, अंतर्राष्ट्रीय समायोजन करने के लिए रुपये को क्या किया गया था? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 1)

Explanation:
1991 में भारत को भुगतान संतुलन के गंभीर संकट का सामना करना पड़ा था। विदेशी मुद्रा भंडार लगभग समाप्त हो गया था। इस स्थिति से निपटने के लिए भारत सरकार ने आर्थिक सुधारों की शुरुआत की, जिसमें रुपये का अवमूल्यन प्रमुख कदम था। रुपये का अवमूल्यन करके निर्यात को प्रोत्साहित किया गया और आयात को महंगा बनाया गया, जिससे व्यापार घाटा कम हुआ। यह कदम अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मुद्रा कोष (IMF) की शर्तों के तहत उठाया गया था। अवमूल्यन से रुपये की वैश्विक बाजार में क्रय शक्ति कम हो गई, लेकिन इससे विदेशी मुद्रा भंडार को स्थिर करने में मदद मिली। यह भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था के उदारीकरण की दिशा में एक महत्वपूर्ण कदम था।

question: How has the advancement of technology impacted employment trends in India?  (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: Technology has uniformly reduced employment opportunities across all sectors
It has created new job opportunities, especially in the IT and service sectors, while also displacing traditional jobs
Only manual and low-skill jobs have been affected by technological advancements
Technological advancement has had no significant impact on employment trends
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It has created new job opportunities, especially in the IT and service sectors, while also displacing traditional jobs

Explanation:
The advancement of technology in India has had a dual impact on employment trends. On one hand, it has created new job opportunities, particularly in the IT and service sectors, increasing demand for skilled workers. On the other hand, automation and digitalization have displaced traditional jobs, especially in manufacturing and agriculture. This has led to a growth in high-skill jobs and a decline in low-skill jobs. Overall, technological progress has altered job dynamics, but the impact is not uniform across all sectors.

question: Which of the following roles does the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) perform in Indian economy? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: Financing and promoting Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)
Managing government pension funds
Regulating foreign exchange transactions
Supervising credit rating agencies
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Financing and promoting Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)

Explanation:
SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India) was established in 1990 by an Act of Parliament. Its primary role is to provide financial assistance and promotion to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). It acts as the apex financial institution for the MSME sector, offering loans, equity, and other services. SIDBI is regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Other options: Managing government pension funds is done by PFRDA; regulating foreign exchange transactions is done by RBI; supervising credit rating agencies is done by SEBI. Thus, SIDBI's role is confined to financing and promoting MSMEs.

question: Which of the following is the 'Utility of a commodity'? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: It is the want of satisfying the capacity of a commodity.
It is the desire to satisfy the capacity of a commodity.
It is the want of dissatisfying the capacity of a commodity.
It is the desire of dissatisfying the capacity of a commodity.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It is the want of satisfying the capacity of a commodity.

Explanation:
In economics, the utility of a commodity refers to its capacity to satisfy a want or desire. It is an inherent property of the good that fulfills a human need. Note that utility is a subjective concept and represents only a capacity, not necessarily actual satisfaction. The term 'want' is more accurate than 'desire' because utility is the ability to satisfy any want, whether basic or complex. Therefore, the correct definition is: Utility of a commodity is its capacity to satisfy a want. The other options are incorrect due to using 'desire' or 'dissatisfying'. Utility is a core concept in consumer theory and helps explain consumer behavior and demand.

☛ What are the types of utility? → Total utility and marginal utility.
☛ Difference between utility and satisfaction? → Utility is capacity; satisfaction is actual experience.

Rural areas also face challenges like low literacy and poor infrastructure, but the regulatory environment remains the biggest hurdle.

question: Which of the following did the conventional method specifically define as 'quasimoney'? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: All forms of money
Media of exchange considered as money
Narrow money
Financial instruments that are not media of exchange but are substitutes
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Financial instruments that are not media of exchange but are substitutes

Explanation:
According to the conventional method, quasimoney refers to financial instruments that are not used as a medium of exchange but serve as substitutes for money. These include savings deposits, time deposits, and money market instruments. Such instruments are liquid and can be easily converted into money, but they are not directly used for transactions. Narrow money (M1) includes only those mediums directly used for exchange, like currency and demand deposits. Quasimoney is part of broad money (M3), which is a broader measure of money supply. Thus, the correct definition is financial instruments that are not media of exchange but are substitutes.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What is the definition of quasimoney? → Financial instruments that are not media of exchange but substitutes
☛ Example of quasimoney? → Savings deposits, time deposits
☛ What is narrow money? → M1 includes currency and demand deposits
☛ What is broad money? → M3 includes M1 and quasimoney
☛ Which money supply includes quasimoney? → Broad money (M3)
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किसको पारंपरिक विधि ने विशेष रूप से 'अर्ध-मुद्रा' (quasimoney) के रूप में परिभाषित किया है? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 3)
options_hi: मुद्रा के सभी रूप

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है वित्तीय साधन जो विनिमय के माध्यम नहीं हैं, लेकिन विकल्प हैं

Explanation:
पारंपरिक विधि के अनुसार, अर्ध-मुद्रा (quasimoney) वे वित्तीय साधन हैं जो विनिमय के माध्यम नहीं हैं, लेकिन मुद्रा के विकल्प के रूप में कार्य करते हैं। इनमें बचत जमा, सावधि जमा, और मुद्रा बाजार के साधन शामिल हैं। ये साधन तरल होते हैं और आसानी से मुद्रा में परिवर्तित किए जा सकते हैं, लेकिन इनका उपयोग सीधे लेन-देन में नहीं होता। संकीर्ण मुद्रा (M1) में केवल वे माध्यम शामिल हैं जो सीधे विनिमय में उपयोग होते हैं, जैसे करेंसी और मांग जमा। अर्ध-मुद्रा को व्यापक मुद्रा (M3) में शामिल किया जाता है, जो मुद्रा आपूर्ति का एक व्यापक माप है।

question: What characterises employment in the informal sector of the Indian economy? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Employment primarily involves self-employment or small, unregistered businesses.
Employment contracts are always written and legally binding.
Workers are entitled to social security benefits and formal job protection.
Informal sector jobs are typically high-wage positions.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Employment primarily involves self-employment or small, unregistered businesses.

Explanation:
The informal sector in India is characterized by self-employment or work in small, unregistered businesses. Employment contracts are typically unwritten and not legally binding. Workers do not receive social security benefits or formal job protection. Wages are generally low, and working conditions are irregular. This sector constitutes a large part of the Indian economy, including agriculture, construction, retail trade, and unorganized parts of the service sector. Informal sector jobs lack legal recognition and are often insecure, with no guaranteed income or benefits.

☛ Percentage of employment in informal sector in India → Approximately 90%.
☛ Major industries in informal sector → Agriculture, construction, domestic work, retail trade.
☛ Main problem of informal sector → Lack of social security and low wages.
☛ Government scheme for informal workers → Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan Yojana.

question: According to the sustainable development approach, which of the following strategies is essential for rural development? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Prioritising short-term economic gains
Focusing solely on agricultural productivity
Increasing reliance on non-renewable resources
Integrating environmental sustainability with economic development
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Integrating environmental sustainability with economic development

Explanation:
Sustainable development means meeting present needs without compromising the ability of future generations. In rural development, focusing only on short-term economic gains or agricultural productivity is unsustainable in the long run. Increasing reliance on non-renewable resources causes environmental damage. The essential strategy is integrating environmental sustainability with economic development, which ensures resource conservation, biodiversity preservation, and strengthens rural livelihoods. This approach ensures that development is balanced environmentally, socially, and economically. It promotes the use of renewable energy, sustainable agriculture, and inclusive growth, leading to long-term resilience of rural communities.

☛ Three Pillars of Sustainable Development → Economic growth, social inclusion, and environmental protection.

☛ SDG 1 (No Poverty) → Promote sustainable livelihoods to eradicate poverty in rural areas.
☛ Use of Renewable Energy → Promote solar, wind, and other renewable sources in rural areas.

question: Which of the following is against globalisation? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 3)

On the other hand, globalisation increases market access, product diversification, and technology use, which are arguments in its favor. question: How does the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) enhance investor protection? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (09/12/2024) Shift 1)

question: When is the Marginal Rate of Substitution (MRS) of Y for X relevant? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (09/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: When the consumer ready to give up both X and Y
When the consumer is ready to give up X for an additional unit of Y
When the consumer acquires additional units of both X and Y
When the consumer is ready to give up Y for an additional unit of X
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is When the consumer is ready to give up X for an additional unit of Y

Explanation:
The Marginal Rate of Substitution (MRS) of Y for X measures the number of units of X that a consumer is willing to give up to obtain one additional unit of Y while remaining on the same indifference curve. This concept is directly linked to the slope of the indifference curve. MRS diminishes as the consumer acquires more of a good due to the law of diminishing marginal utility. It is relevant only when the consumer substitutes X for Y, not when giving up both or acquiring both.

☛ Which curve is MRS related to? → Indifference curve.
☛ Why does MRS diminish? → Due to the law of diminishing marginal utility.
☛ MRS for perfect substitutes? → Constant.
☛ MRS for perfect complements? → Infinite or zero.

question: In which of the following ways can the utility be expressed in cardinal utility analysis? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (09/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: In numbers
In quality
In rank
In order
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is In numbers

Explanation:
In cardinal utility analysis, utility is expressed in numerical values (e.g., 1, 2, 3). It assumes that utility can be measured and compared. For example, a person might say that an apple gives them 10 units of utility and an orange gives 5, indicating that apple's utility is twice that of orange. This approach was proposed by Alfred Marshall and is used in the theory of consumer behavior. In contrast, ordinal utility analysis expresses utility in rank or order.

question: Which of the following census years reported the highest sex ratio in India? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (09/12/2024) Shift 2)

solution:

Explanation:
According to the Indian census, the highest sex ratio was recorded in 1901 with 972 females per 1000 males. After that, it steadily declined to 943 in 2011. question: Which of the following is the correct function of marketed surplus? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (09/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: Marketed Surplus = Total demand in the market - Total supply
Marketed Surplus = Total supply of the market - Total demand
Marketed Surplus = Total farm output produced by the farmer - Own consumption of farm output
Marketed Surplus = Total farm produce - Previous years stock in the market
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Marketed Surplus = Total farm output produced by the farmer - Own consumption of farm output

Explanation:
Marketed surplus refers to the portion of a farmer's total output that is sold in the market after deducting own consumption. It is calculated as total farm output minus own consumption. This concept is crucial in agricultural economics as it indicates the quantity of farm produce available for sale in the market. It helps measure the marketable surplus after harvest. The other options involve market demand and supply or previous stocks, which do not correctly define marketed surplus at the farmer level. Understanding this definition is essential for analyzing agricultural markets and farmer income.
